title: Toad in the Hole
subtitle: Chorizo baked in Yorkshire pudding batter
excerpt: Sliced chorizo baked in a puffed-up Yorkshire pudding batter with a quick onion gravy on the side. This is proper British comfort food that rewards a very hot oven.
sourceNotes: Adapted from the classic British toad in the hole using chorizo in place of traditional pork sausages.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the batter up to 1 hour ahead and let it rest at room temperature.
recipe.temperatureNote: 200C fan. The oven must be fully up to temperature before adding the batter.

content.text: The fat in the tin must be smoking hot before the batter goes in. This is what makes the batter rise and puff up around the edges.
Whisk the flour, eggs, and milk together to make a smooth batter. Season with salt. Set aside.
Pour the oil into a large roasting tin. Place in the oven for 10 minutes until the oil is smoking.
Add the chorizo slices to the hot tin. Return to the oven for 5 minutes.
Working quickly, pour the batter around the chorizo. Drop the thyme sprigs over. Close the oven door fast.
Bake for 25 minutes without opening the oven. The batter should be puffed, golden, and set.
While it bakes, fry the onion in a little oil for 12 minutes until very soft and golden.
Add the stock and mustard to the onion. Simmer for 8 minutes until slightly reduced. Season to taste.
Rest the toad in the hole for 5 minutes before serving with the gravy.

items.cause: Fat was not hot enough or oven door opened too soon.
items.fix: Ensure fat is smoking before pouring and do not open the oven.

items.symptom: Batter is soggy in the middle.
items.cause: Tin was too deep or batter too thick.
items.fix: Return to oven for 5 more minutes uncovered.

items.symptom: Chorizo has shrunk and gone dry.
items.cause: Pre-cooked in the tin for too long.
items.fix: Add chorizo at the same time as the batter next time.
